meaning: A thin sheet with dark ink or dye on one side. Placed between two pages, it made a copy of what you wrote or typed.
clues: It is a thin sheet of paper, not a machine.
One side is coated with dark ink or dye that rubs off.
You slid it between two sheets, with the coated side facing down.
When you wrote or typed on the top sheet, a copy appeared on the one below.
It has two words. The first has six letters and starts with C. The second is what you write on.
assumes: A typewriter prints letters one key at a time
A mimeograph copies a page using a stencil

decoys.meaning: A machine with a keyboard that presses letters onto paper, one key at a time.
A machine that scans a paper page and sends a copy over a phone line. Another machine prints the copy.
An old copier. Ink is pushed through a typed stencil, so one page can be copied again and again.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, a typist slid a sheet of this between pages and got a copy for free. Smudgy fingers came with it.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Today's version: copy and paste, or the "cc" line in an email. The "cc" still stands for carbon copy!
